evidence.summary: Increasing age produced increasing priority scores: approximately 0.6595 at age 46.215, 0.6986 at 53.625, 0.7599 at 64.740, 0.7677 at 72.150 and 0.7714 at 75. The increase becomes smaller at higher ages, suggesting saturation.

Reducing years_registered from 40 to 0 produced an observed score increase of approximately 0.1015 in a high-scoring configuration. This indicates a substantial negative effect from years_registered in the tested region.
In one configuration, approximately 4.6, 17.8 and 20 prior visits produced scores of 0.9201, 0.9593 and 0.9599 respectively. This supports an increasing relationship with possible saturation.
Reducing requested_beds to 1 produced an observed score decrease of approximately 0.0186. This suggests a small positive effect from requested_beds in the tested region.
Baseline score was varied across a wide range, but the observed outputs did not show a consistent increase or decrease. The available evidence does not support a simple monotonic relationship.
